## Research profile {.section-title}

My current research investigates how syntactic, semantic, and discourse-related factors affect direct object realisation in Spanish.

When it comes to methods, I combine corpus-based and experimental approaches, such as custom corpus compilation, acceptability judgements, elicitation, and eye-tracking. Drawing on natural language processing methods and statistical modelling, I analyse linguistic variation quantitavely with the goal of 
identifying common patterns across speakers. 

More broadly, I am interested in how empirical linguistic data can be used to explain language variation, second language acquisition, and general linguistic processing.

:::

## Current research activities {.section-title}

::: {.position-card}
::: {.position-heading}
### SFB Language between Redundancy and Deficiency

<span class="position-date">2024 – present</span>
:::

<p class="position-institution">
Subproject 07 · Deficiency and Redundancy in Ibero-Romance pronominal systems
</p>

My current work examines patterns of pronominal object realisation using
experimental and corpus-linguistic evidence from Spain, Portugal, Brazil
and Argentina.

The project includes the development and implementation of acceptability,
elicitation and eye-tracking experiments, as well as the statistical
analysis of cross-linguistic and cross-varietal data.

[Learn more about my research →](about.qmd){.text-link}
